> When adapting this to another IDP, the residue span in `assignment.txt` is the consistency check point: column 3 minus column 2 plus one must equal the residue count under that chain's header in `protein.seq`, or the pool generation operates on an inconsistent definition. The tutorial pair (`A 1 26` ↔ 26 residues) is the minimal verified reference configuration.

Sources: [Example_tutorial/assignment.txt](Example_tutorial/assignment.txt#L1), [Example_tutorial/protein.seq](Example_tutorial/protein.seq#L1-L2)

## Running RANCH: Command, Parameters, and Output

The tutorial runs RANCH from inside `Example_tutorial/` after creating an output directory. The full invocation is a single command with three options and the two positional files:

```bash
mkdir pool_20

ranch --repetitions 20 --prefix pool_20/model_ \
    --seed 12345 assignment.txt protein.seq
```

The README documents the result precisely: "`pool_20/` containing 20 randomly generated conformations in CIF format". Note the CIF output format (not PDB) — downstream steps reference CIF files explicitly, and the plotting utilities in step 4 also glob for `*.cif` when identifying GAJOE's selected structures.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L38-L47), [README.md](README.md#L100-L117)

| CLI element | Tutorial value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `--repetitions` | `20` | Number of conformations in the generated pool |
| `--prefix` | `pool_20/model_` | Output directory combined with filename stem; each conformation is written as `model_N.cif` inside `pool_20/` |
| `--seed` | `12345` | Deterministic seed for the random generator — the same seed regenerates the identical pool |
| positional arg 1 | `assignment.txt` | Chain/residue layout declaration |
| positional arg 2 | `protein.seq` | Per-chain sequence definition |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L40-L45), [README.md](README.md#L47)

RANCH requires an ATSAS installation, which is the same external dependency as the rest of the EOM pipeline (the README recommends GAJOE v2.1 for ease of use). Installation guidance is on [Software Requirements and Installation](3-software-requirements-and-installation), and the full worked sequence including GAJOE is on [EOM Tutorial with ATSAS Tools](4-eom-tutorial-with-atsas-tools).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L22-L24), [README.md](README.md#L34)

## Output Artifacts and Downstream Traceability

The pool directory is not a throwaway intermediate — the repository's analysis scripts depend on being able to match GAJOE's selected structures back to the pool by **filename stem**. This creates a traceability contract that spans three stages:

1. RANCH writes `pool_20/model_N.cif` using the `--prefix` stem.
2. FFMAKER consumes the glob `pool_20/*.cif` and records each conformation's name in `size_statistics_20.csv` (the tutorial's step 2; the README also notes you can substitute provided PDB structures in place of the generated pool for that analysis).
3. `2d.py` reads the pool statistics, globs GAJOE's selected structures (`GA001/curve_1/pdbs/*.cif`), builds a boolean mask by comparing file stems, and **asserts** that every selected structure was found in the pool — raising `"Some selected structures were not found in the pool!"` otherwise.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L51-L60), [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L8-L31), [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L36-L41)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["RANCH:<br/>pool_20/model_N.cif"] -->|"glob *.cif"| FM["FFMAKER:<br/>size_statistics_20.csv<br/>(names per row)"]
    FM -->|"names + Rg/Ree"| D["2d.py"]
    R --> GA["GAJOE"]
    GA -->|"pdbs/*.cif<br/>(selected stems)"| D
    D --> ASSERT["mask = name in selected_names<br/>assert mask.sum() == len(selected_names)"]
```

The practical consequence for a developer adapting this workflow: once a pool is generated and fed to FFMAKER, its directory name and filename stems are load-bearing identifiers. Renaming pool files between generation and analysis breaks the `2d.py` assertion and silently corrupts the pool-versus-selection comparison.

> [!TIP]
> The stem-matching assert in `2d.py` (lines 40–41) is the repository's only automated check that the GAJOE selection and the pool statistics describe the same conformational set. If you regenerate the pool with a different seed but reuse an old `size_statistics_20.csv`, the assert can still pass while comparing inconsistent populations — regenerate the FFMAKER statistics together with the pool.

Sources: [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L27-L31), [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L40-L41)

## Pool Design: Reproducibility versus Statistical Power

The tutorial's 20-conformation pool exists to demonstrate mechanics, not to support quantitative conclusions. The README states this constraint twice, in both directions: the GAJOE settings are "intended for a quick demonstration" and the pool itself is "intended only to demonstrate the workflow. Quantitative ensemble analysis requires substantially larger, adequately sampled conformational pools."

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L85-L89), [README.md](README.md#L118)

| Aspect | Tutorial pool | Production pool |
|---|---|---|
| `--repetitions` | 20 | "sufficiently large" pool for quantitative analysis |
| Purpose | Demonstrate the RANCH → FFMAKER → GAJOE → plotting sequence | Statistically meaningful ensemble distributions |
| GAJOE budget paired with it | 1 run × 100 generations, ensemble 1–10 | More independent runs and generations (README's explicit recommendation) |
| Interpreting outputs | Shape of workflow only | Distributions of Rg, Dmax, Ree comparable to experiment |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L62-L89), [README.md](README.md#L118)

The `--seed 12345` parameter is the mechanism that makes the small pool a stable benchmark artifact: every execution with the same seed and inputs yields byte-identical conformations, so the tutorial is reproducible across machines. When you scale up for real analysis, keep the seed discipline — record the seed alongside the pool so that a published ensemble can be regenerated exactly, while selecting a pool size large enough that the random sampling adequately covers conformational space.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L40-L45), [README.md](README.md#L118)

The downstream interpretation of pool-derived distributions — and how GAJOE selects a sub-ensemble from them — continues in [GAJOE Genetic Algorithm Ensemble Fitting](8-gajoe-genetic-algorithm-ensemble-fitting), with a field-by-field description of GAJOE's result files in [GAJOE Output File Reference](9-gajoe-output-file-reference).

## Next Steps

The natural reading progression after this page follows the pipeline's execution order: [FFMAKER Theoretical SAXS Profiles](7-ffmaker-theoretical-saxs-profiles) documents how the generated CIF pool is converted into theoretical intensity and size-statistics files, then [GAJOE Genetic Algorithm Ensemble Fitting](8-gajoe-genetic-algorithm-ensemble-fitting) covers the fitting stage that consumes both. For the complete worked command sequence in one place, see [EOM Tutorial with ATSAS Tools](4-eom-tutorial-with-atsas-tools). If your goal is to supply pools from simulation rather than random generation, proceed to [MD Ensemble Generation with AMBER](18-md-ensemble-generation-with-amber); for the biological context of the 26-residue sequence used here, see [H4 Histone Tail Case Study](17-h4-histone-tail-case-study).


# FFMAKER Theoretical SAXS Profiles



FFMAKER is the ATSAS stage that converts raw structural coordinates into the *language GAJOE speaks*: per-conformer theoretical small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) intensity profiles, I(q). This page explains FFMAKER's role in the EOM pipeline as exercised in this repository, its exact input/output contract as invoked by the tutorial, how its output is resampled against experimental data, and how the theoretical-profile lineage can be traced all the way into the MATLAB and Python analysis scripts. For pool *generation* (RANCH) and genetic *fitting* (GAJOE), see their dedicated pages.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L49-L60), [README.md](README.md#L10-L13)

## Where FFMAKER Sits in the Pipeline

FFMAKER occupies the middle of the three-stage EOM workflow: it consumes the conformational pool emitted by RANCH and produces the two artifacts — theoretical intensities and size statistics — that GAJOE requires as its search space and fitness landscape. Conceptually, it is the *simulation-to-scattering bridge*: each disordered conformation sampled from MD or generated de novo becomes one computable scattering curve, turning a structural ensemble question ("which conformations exist?") into an intensity-ensemble question ("which weighted sum of curves reproduces the measurement?").

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph IN["Structural pool"]
        MD["MD / PDB ensemble"]
        R["RANCH<br/>pool_20/*.cif"]
    end
    F["FFMAKER<br/>CRYSOL-based I(q) per conformer"]
    subgraph ART["FFMAKER artifacts"]
        I["intensities_20.csv<br/>theoretical I(q), all conformers"]
        S["size_statistics_20.csv<br/>Rg, Dmax, Ree, volume"]
    end
    E["H4WT_150Na.dat<br/>experimental target"]
    G["GAJOE<br/>genetic ensemble fit"]
    O["GA001/curve_1/<br/>profiles_001_1.fit, GA_CYCLE_*.txt"]
    A["MATLAB / Python analysis<br/>plotEOMSAXScomparison.m, graph.py, getBestCurve.m"]

    MD --> R
    R --> F
    F --> I
    F --> S
    I --> G
    S --> G
    E --> G
    G --> O
    O --> A
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L38-L47), [README.md](README.md#L49-L60), [README.md](README.md#L62-L74)

## The FFMAKER Input/Output Contract

The tutorial invokes FFMAKER with two flags and a file glob:

```bash
ffmaker --output intensities_20.csv \
    --pool size_statistics_20.csv pool_20/*.cif
```

FFMAKER is deliberately agnostic about where the coordinates come from: it accepts RANCH-generated CIF files, and the README notes that user-provided PDB structures (e.g., MD snapshots) can be substituted by replacing `pool_20/*.cif` with the path to those files. This is exactly the entry point this repository exploits for its benchmarking purpose — MD ensembles generated with AMBER enter the SAXS pipeline here, not at RANCH.

| Element | Role | Verified content |
|---|---|---|
| `pool_20/*.cif` (positional) | Input conformations | RANCH output pool, one structure file per conformation |
| PDB paths (alternative) | Input conformations | MD-derived or user-supplied structures |
| `--output intensities_20.csv` | Theoretical intensities | "theoretical SAXS intensity profiles for all conformations" |
| `--pool size_statistics_20.csv` | Size statistics | Per-conformation **R_g**, **D_max**, end-to-end distance (**R_ee**), and **volume** |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L49-L60), [README.md](README.md#L56-L58)

## Theoretical vs. Experimental Profiles

Understanding FFMAKER means understanding what its output must eventually compete against. The repository ships the experimental counterpart in `SAXSData/`: a 4-line header (`### DATA:`, point count `53`, column legend `Q I(Q) Error`) followed by 53 evenly spaced points covering q ≈ 1.56×10⁻² to 2.96×10⁻¹ Å⁻¹ (spacing ≈ 5.4×10⁻³ Å⁻¹). The two artifact families differ in every property that matters downstream:

| Property | FFMAKER theoretical profile | Experimental `.dat` (`H4WT_150Na.dat`) |
|---|---|---|
| Origin | Computation from atomic coordinates (CRYSOL lineage) | SAXS measurement |
| Content | One I(q) curve **per conformation** in the pool | A single measured curve |
| Uncertainty | None | Per-point σ column |
| q-grid | FFMAKER-native (see resampling below) | 53 points, q ∈ [0.0156, 0.296] Å⁻¹ |
| Pipeline role | GAJOE's search space | GAJOE's fitting target |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L56-L58), [SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat](SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat#L1-L5), [SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat](SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat#L50-L57)

## Handoff to GAJOE: The Fitting Interface

GAJOE consumes both FFMAKER artifacts through explicitly named flags — `--intensity intensities_20.csv` ("theoretical SAXS profiles calculated by FFMAKER") and `--size size_statistics_20.csv` ("structural properties of the conformations") — while the experimental `.dat` is passed as the final positional argument. This flag naming makes the data lineage unambiguous: intensities define what GAJOE can *add up* (weighted sums of theoretical curves), size statistics define what GAJOE can *report* (R_g, D_max, R_ee distributions of the selected ensemble), and the experimental curve defines what GAJOE optimizes against.

> [!TIP]
> The theoretical q-grid never survives into the fit: `profiles_001_1.fit` contains **exactly 53 data rows** — one per experimental point — and its q column matches the `.dat` values to rounding precision (e.g., `1.563542e-002` vs `1.56E-02`). Downstream scripts can therefore treat column 1 of any `.fit` file as *the experimental q-grid*, regardless of how FFMAKER sampled I(q) internally.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L62-L87), [SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat](SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat#L1-L5)

## Anatomy of the Fitted Profile: `profiles_*.fit`

GAJOE's fit files are where FFMAKER's theoretical curves re-emerge in human-readable form. The first line is a metadata header; the remaining 53 rows are four aligned channels on the experimental q-grid. Both shipped consumers decode the file identically: the MATLAB script reads it with `NumHeaderLines=1` and extracts `fitFile(:,4)` into a variable tellingly named `crysolEOM`, while the Python tutorial unpacks `q, exp, err, fit = data[:, :4].T`. The `crysolEOM` naming corroborates the CRYSOL lineage documented for EOM in the README ("GAJOE, which uses CRYSOL").

| File region | Column / field | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Header line | `CYCLE: 29` | GA cycle (run) that produced the reported fit |
| Header line | `Chi^2: 1.226` | Fit quality of the reported ensemble |
| Header line | `GENER.: 1000`, `ENSEMBLES: 50` | Optimization budget (case-study scale, vs. the tutorial's 100/20) |
| Header line | `CURVES: 9` | Number of conformers in the winning ensemble |
| Data rows | 1 | q — experimental grid (Å⁻¹) |
| Data rows | 2 | Experimental I(q) |
| Data rows | 3 | Uncertainty channel as recorded in the fit |
| Data rows | 4 | **Fitted ensemble intensity — the weighted sum of FFMAKER's theoretical curves** |

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph FF["FFMAKER: intensities_20.csv"]
        C1["conformer 1 I(q)"]
        C2["conformer 2 I(q)"]
        CN["conformer N I(q)"]
    end
    W["GAJOE selects & weights<br/>ensemble of k conformers"]
    FIT["profiles_001_1.fit<br/>col 1: q (experimental grid)<br/>col 2: I_exp<br/>col 3: uncertainty<br/>col 4: ensemble I_theor"]
    M["plotEOMSAXScomparison.m<br/>fitFile(:,4)"]
    P["graph.py<br/>data[:, 3]"]
    IDX["GA_CYCLE_*.txt<br/>conformer index stream"]
    BC["getBestCurve.m<br/>index → frequency table"]

    C1 --> W
    C2 --> W
    CN --> W
    W --> FIT
    FIT --> M
    FIT --> P
    W -. records indices .-> IDX
    IDX --> BC
```

Sources: [ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit#L1-L2), [plotEOMSAXScomparison.m](plotEOMSAXScomparison.m#L18-L21), [graph.py](Example_tutorial/graph.py#L26-L31), [README.md](README.md#L10-L13), [README.md](README.md#L93)

## Conformer Index Traceability Back to FFMAKER's Pool Order

GAJOE never re-references structures by filename in its logs — it identifies conformers by **integer index**, and those indices are positions in the pool ordering that FFMAKER processed. Each line of `GA_CYCLE_*.txt` records a generation, a χ² rank, and the winning ensemble as a dash-delimited index stream (e.g., `-156-359-734-792-792-805-812-1159-1166`). `getBestCurve.m` exploits this by parsing all cycle files with `-` as the delimiter and tabulating how frequently each index appears across runs, producing the `[PDB number, frequency]` table that recreates GAJOE 1.3's removed `best_curve.txt`. The case study's consistency checks confirm the mapping: indices reach 1994 in `GA_CYCLE_1.txt` while `Size_list.txt` retains exactly 2000 per-conformer rows of (index, R_g, D_max) — matching the ~2000-conformer MD pool behind the published analysis.

> [!TIP]
> Index-to-structure mapping depends on **file ordering at FFMAKER invocation time**. Shell glob expansion (`pool_20/*.cif`) is lexicographic and stable on a given system, but if you regenerate or rename pool files between the FFMAKER run and any downstream index interpretation, `getBestCurve.m` frequencies will silently point at the wrong structures. Keep the pool directory immutable after FFMAKER runs.

Sources: [ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L2), [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L16-L35), [ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L15)

## Practical Considerations

Three verified observations calibrate expectations when running FFMAKER in this workflow. First, **pool scale matters**: the tutorial's 20-conformation run is explicitly flagged as a workflow demonstration only, with the README noting that quantitative ensemble analysis requires substantially larger, adequately sampled pools — the shipped case study used ~2000 conformers and a proportionally larger GA budget (1000 generations, 50 candidate ensembles per generation, vs. the tutorial's 100/20). Second, **input format flexibility is the MD-entry point**: replacing the CIF glob with PDB paths is the documented mechanism for feeding simulation ensembles into the scattering pipeline. Third, **the size-statistics artifact is not optional bookkeeping** — GAJOE derives every structural distribution it reports (R_g, D_max, R_ee) from the `--pool` file, so FFMAKER's second output directly shapes the ensemble descriptors analyzed in later pages.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L118-L118), [README.md](README.md#L60-L60), [README.md](README.md#L80-L80)

## Summary and Next Steps

FFMAKER's contract in this repository is compact but load-bearing: take a pool of conformations (RANCH CIFs or MD PDBs), emit one theoretical I(q) per conformer plus a size-statistics table, and hand both to GAJOE. Its influence persists through the entire output chain — resampled onto the experimental q-grid in `profiles_*.fit` column 4, and addressable by pool-order index in `GA_CYCLE_*.txt`. Natural continuation points from here: how the pool itself is generated in [RANCH Conformational Pool Generation](6-ranch-conformational-pool-generation), how the theoretical curves are genetically recombined in [GAJOE Genetic Algorithm Ensemble Fitting](8-gajoe-genetic-algorithm-ensemble-fitting), a file-by-file breakdown in [GAJOE Output File Reference](9-gajoe-output-file-reference), how ensemble averages are reconstructed in [Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles](10-best-curve-reconstruction-from-ga-cycles) and [SAXS Fit, Kratky Plot, and Residuals](13-saxs-fit-kratky-plot-and-residuals), and the physical meaning of the size descriptors FFMAKER emits in [Structural Descriptors: Rg, Dmax, Ree](16-structural-descriptors-rg-dmax-ree).


# GAJOE Genetic Algorithm Ensemble Fitting



GAJOE is the ensemble-fitting engine of the EOM pipeline: it takes a pool of theoretical SAXS profiles plus per-conformation structural descriptors, and runs a genetic algorithm that discovers which small subset of conformations, when averaged, reproduces an experimental SAXS curve. This page explains GAJOE's role in this repository, its command-line contract, the genetic algorithm mechanics as recorded in real output logs, and the exact file formats downstream analysis scripts depend on. All evidence is drawn from the shipped example output in `ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/` and the parsing code that consumes it.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L11-L12), [README.md](README.md#L15-L17)

## Position in the EOM Pipeline

GAJOE is the third and decisive stage of the EOM chain. RANCH generates the conformational pool, FFMAKER converts that pool into per-conformation theoretical intensities and a size-statistics table, and GAJOE then searches that pool for the sub-ensemble that best matches experiment. It consumes three inputs — FFMAKER's intensity file, FFMAKER's size statistics, and an experimental `.dat` profile — and produces an output directory (`GA001`, `GA002`, …) whose artifacts feed every downstream MATLAB and Python analysis script in this repository. The repository's README explicitly delegates the tool's internal documentation to the ATSAS manual, noting that GAJOE computes profiles through CRYSOL, so this page documents the tool *through its observable interface and outputs* as they appear here.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["RANCH<br/>conformational pool"] --> F["FFMAKER<br/>intensities_*.csv + size_statistics_*.csv"]
    F --> G["GAJOE<br/>genetic algorithm ensemble fitting"]
    E["Experimental SAXS<br/>H4WT_150Na.dat"] --> G
    G --> O["GA001/curve_1/<br/>.fit · distributions · GA_CYCLE logs · pdbs/"]
    O --> M["MATLAB &amp; Python analysis scripts"]
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L11-L13), [README.md](README.md#L15-L18)

The experimental input that anchors the fit is a standard three-column SAXS dataset (`Q`, `I(Q)`, `Error`) with four header lines, of which 53 q-points are used. GAJOE scores every candidate ensemble directly against these measured intensities and errors.

Sources: [SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat](SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat#L1-L5)

## Running GAJOE: Command-Line Contract

The tutorial's runnable invocation shows the full CLI surface. The first positional argument is the experimental data file; all pool inputs and algorithm controls are passed as flags. Note that the tutorial's `--times 1 --generation 100` values are deliberately minimal for a quick demonstration — the shipped ExampleData run used substantially larger settings (100 runs × 1000 generations), as its outputs prove.

```bash
gajoe \
    --intensity intensities_20.csv \
    --size size_statistics_20.csv \
    --times 1 \
    --generation 100 \
    --ensemble 20 \
    --minimum 1 \
    --maximum 10 \
    --no-repeated \
    H4WT_150Na.dat
```

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L62-L75)

| Flag | Tutorial value | Meaning | ExampleData evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--intensity` | `intensities_20.csv` | FFMAKER theoretical SAXS profiles per conformation | — |
| `--size` | `size_statistics_20.csv` | Per-conformation Rg, Dmax, Ree, volume | `Size_list.txt` holds the 2000-row pool table |
| `--times` | `1` | Number of independent GA runs | 100 `GA_CYCLE_N.txt` files exist |
| `--generation` | `100` | Generations per run | Each log records 1000 generations |
| `--ensemble` | `20` | Candidate ensembles evaluated per generation | 20 ranked entries per generation in logs |
| `--minimum` | `1` | Minimum conformations in the selected ensemble | Final ensembles span ~5–15 members |
| `--maximum` | `10` | Maximum conformations in the selected ensemble | Some ensembles exceed 10 (repeat mode) |
| `--no-repeated` | flag | Forbids duplicate conformations within one ensemble | *Not* used in the ExampleData run — winning ensembles repeat indices |
| positional | `H4WT_150Na.dat` | Experimental SAXS data to fit | 53 q-points |

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L77-L87), [README.md](README.md#L89-L89)

> [!TIP]
> For quantitative work, the README itself warns that the tutorial's small pool and few generations are for workflow demonstration only — increase generations, independent runs, and pool size before trusting χ² values. The ExampleData directory is what a production-scale run looks like: 100 runs at 1000 generations each.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L89-L89), [README.md](README.md#L118-L118)

## The Genetic Algorithm at Work: Evidence from GA_CYCLE Logs

The most granular window into GAJOE's behavior is the `GA_CYCLE_N.txt` family — one file per independent GA run (N = 1…100 here), each containing the complete ranked population for every generation. The format is two-column-header (`Gener Best`) followed by one line per candidate: generation number, rank within the generation (1 = best), the candidate's χ² fitness, and its ensemble composition as a dash-delimited list of pool indices. Run 1's log is exactly 20,002 lines: 1,000 generations × 20 ranked candidates, plus header — confirming the population-size semantics of `--ensemble` and `--generation`.

Sources: [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L21), [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L14-L16)

The fitness trajectory shows textbook GA convergence. In run 1, generation 1, the population's χ² spans 16.43 to 35.26 — a wide, poorly adapted spread. By the final generation of run 29 (the run GAJOE ultimately selected), the entire population has homogenized into a narrow band of χ² 1.23–1.27, and the top-ranked candidate's composition is dominated by repeated selections of just four pool indices (`1093, 1592, 1623, 1734`). That repetition is direct evidence of selection pressure: conformations that individually improve the fit get amplified across the ensemble, which is only possible because this run was executed *without* the `--no-repeated` flag that the tutorial uses.

Sources: [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L2-L21), [GA_CYCLE_29.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_29.txt#L19981-L20001)

| Snapshot | Location | Best χ² | Population spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| Run 1, generation 1 | [GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L21](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L21) | 16.43 | 16.43 – 35.26 |
| Run 29, generation 1000 | [GA_CYCLE_29.txt#L20001](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_29.txt#L20001) | 1.23 | 1.23 – 1.27 |
| Winning-run header (exact) | [profiles_001_1.fit#L1](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit#L1) | 1.226 | — |

Because `--times` controls independent restarts, GAJOE's final answer is a *best-of-runs* selection. The `.fit` file header records this as `CYCLE: 29` — run 29 won among the 100 restarts with χ² 1.226, with `GENER.:1000 ENSEMBLES: 50 CURVES: 9` summarizing the optimization settings used. Independent restarts matter precisely because each GA run converges to a different local optimum: compare run 1's final best ensemble (`-156-359-734-792-805-812-1159-1166`-family indices, run 1 file) against run 100's (`-729-1093-1592-1623` family in run 29, different again in run 100's log).

Sources: [profiles_001_1.fit](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit#L1-L1), [GA_CYCLE_100.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_100.txt#L1-L21)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Start run n<br/>random population of<br/>candidate ensembles"] --> B["Average FFMAKER curves<br/>per candidate ensemble"]
    B --> C["Score against experimental<br/>chi^2 fitness"]
    C --> D["Rank population<br/>1 best ... 20 worst"]
    D --> E["Next generation<br/>fitter ensembles dominate"]
    E --> F{"Generation 1000<br/>reached?"}
    F -- "no" --> B
    F -- "yes" --> G["Write full history<br/>GA_CYCLE_n.txt"]
    G --> H{"Best of all<br/>100 runs?"}
    H -- "yes: CYCLE 29" --> I["profiles_001_1.fit<br/>chi^2 1.226"]
```

> [!TIP]
> χ² drops roughly 13× from a random first-generation population (16.43) to the converged optimum (1.23), and the final generation's population spread collapses from ~19 χ² units to 0.04 — use this spread as a quick convergence diagnostic when tuning `--generation` for your own pools.

Sources: [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L2-L21), [GA_CYCLE_29.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_29.txt#L19982-L20001)

## The GA_CYCLE Workfile Contract

The `GA_CYCLE` files are not part of GAJOE's default output — `getBestCurve.m` documents that they only appear when you answer **yes** to GAJOE v2–3's interactive prompt *"Save workfiles with the entire GA runs? (default: no)"*. Without them, this repository's analysis chain loses its main input, because GAJOE v2 removed the `best_curve.txt` file that version 1.3 used to emit. `getBestCurve.m` reconstructs that lost artifact: it reads every `GA_CYCLE_N.txt` using `-` as the column delimiter (which splits ensemble indices cleanly), keeps only the last `curvesPerEnsemble` lines of each run — the final generation's ranked population — and tabulates how often each pool index was selected across all runs.

Sources: [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L3-L12), [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L19-L30)

The frequency table it returns is what turns GA logs into science: a pool index that appears in many final-generation ensembles across 100 independent runs is robustly selected, whereas one appearing in a single lucky run is noise. This is why `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` asks you to declare `nRuns` (what you told GAJOE for "Number of times you want the genetic algorithm repeated") and `curvesPerEnsemble` (what you entered for "Maximum number of curves per ensemble") — those two numbers parameterize the parsing of the very same prompts GAJOE asked during setup.

Sources: [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L31-L39), [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L15-L16)

## Output Artifact Reference

A completed GAJOE run deposits everything downstream scripts need into `GA001/curve_1/`. The following table maps every artifact observed in the shipped example to its verified format.

| Artifact | Count | Verified format |
|---|---|---|
| `GA_CYCLE_N.txt` | 100 | Header `Gener Best` + 1,000 generations × 20 ranked candidates (χ² + ensemble indices) |
| `profiles_001_1.fit` | 1 | Header (`CYCLE/Chi²/GENER./ENSEMBLES/CURVES`) + 53 rows of `q, I_exp, σ, I_fit` |
| `Rg_distr_001_1.txt` | 1 | 4 summary lines + 54-bin table: `Rg, Pool freq., Sel. freq.` |
| `Size_distr_001_1.txt` | 1 | Same structure for Dmax |
| `CaCa_distr_001_1.txt` | 1 | Same structure for Ca(N)–Ca(C) distance — **zero-filled** here |
| `Volume_distr_001_1.txt` | 1 | Same structure for volume — **zero-filled** here |
| `Size_list.txt` | 1 | 2,000 rows: `pool index, Rg, Dmax` |
| `Ree_values.mat` | 1 | MATLAB array `R` (end-to-end distances, computed externally per script header) |
| `pdbs/`, `logFile_*.log` | — | Selected conformations; optimization settings — documented for tutorial runs |

Sources: [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L2), [profiles_001_1.fit](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit#L1-L2), [Rg_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Rg_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L6), [Size_list.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L3), [README.md](README.md#L91-L98), [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L1-L4)

Two artifacts deserve special attention. First, `Size_list.txt` contains exactly 2,000 data rows — one per pool conformation with its Rg and Dmax — and its index range (up to 1994) matches the maximum index observed inside `GA_CYCLE` ensemble strings; this is the join key that maps abstract pool indices back to physical descriptors. Second, `CaCa_distr` and `Volume_distr` files exist but are entirely zero-filled: when the FFMAKER input lacked those descriptors, GAJOE still emits the files with empty histograms rather than omitting them, so downstream code must tolerate degenerate distributions.

Sources: [Size_list.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L15), [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L4-L8), [CaCa_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/CaCa_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L12), [Volume_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Volume_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L12)

## The Fit File: Format and Physical Result

`profiles_001_1.fit` is the single most consumed GAJOE artifact. Its one-line header packs the winning run's metadata (`CYCLE: 29  Chi^2: 1.226  GENER.:1000  ENSEMBLES: 50  CURVES:  9`), and its 53 data rows carry four columns: q, experimental intensity, experimental error, and the ensemble-averaged fitted intensity. The q-grid matches the experimental dataset point-for-point, because the fit is evaluated exactly where data exists. The repository's two independent consumers agree on this layout: `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m` reads the file with one header line and takes columns 1 and 4 as the fitted (q, I) pair, while `graph.py` unpacks all four columns as `q, exp, err, fit`.

Sources: [profiles_001_1.fit](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit#L1-L2), [plotEOMSAXScomparison.m](plotEOMSAXScomparison.m#L16-L28), [graph.py](Example_tutorial/graph.py#L24-L31)

Beyond the curve itself, the distribution files quantify *what kind* of conformations the GA selected versus what the MD pool contained. The answer for H4-WT is a systematic shift toward extended states: the selected ensemble's average Rg is 15.27 Å against the pool's 13.77 Å, and its average Dmax is 47.33 Å against 42.69 Å. Each distribution file also reports the histogram-mode values separately from the arithmetic average, and provides paired `Pool freq.` / `Sel. freq.` columns so the shift can be plotted directly as overlapping histograms.

Sources: [Rg_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Rg_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L5), [Size_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L5)

| Descriptor | Pool average | Selected ensemble average | Shift |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rg | 13.77 Å | 15.27 Å | +1.50 Å |
| Dmax | 42.69 Å | 47.33 Å | +4.64 Å |

Sources: [Rg_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Rg_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L4), [Size_distr_001_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L4)

## Downstream Consumption Map

Every analysis entry point in the repository starts from a GAJOE output directory. `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` joins three artifacts: selection frequencies from `getBestCurve(dir, nRuns, curvesPerEnsemble)`, per-pool Rg/Dmax from `Size_list.txt`, and end-to-end distances from `Ree_values.mat` (loaded as variable `R`); it then replicates each selected structure's descriptors by its selection frequency to build the SAXS-refined ensemble's joint (Ree, Rg, Dmax) distribution. `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m` overlays the `.fit` file's column-4 fitted curve against the experimental data from `SAXSData/`, including Kratky and residual views. The Python side mirrors this: `graph.py` plots the fit and the three distribution files, and `2d.py` identifies GAJOE's chosen conformations by matching filenames in `GA001/curve_1/pdbs/` against the FFMAKER size-statistics table.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L30-L55), [plotEOMSAXScomparison.m](plotEOMSAXScomparison.m#L15-L45), [graph.py](Example_tutorial/graph.py#L39-L50), [2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L8-L38)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    G["GAJOE output<br/>GA001/curve_1/"] --> C1["GA_CYCLE_*.txt"]
    G --> C2["profiles_001_1.fit"]
    G --> C3["*_distr_*.txt"]
    G --> C4["Size_list.txt"]
    G --> C5["pdbs/"]
    C1 --> P1["getBestCurve.m<br/>selection frequencies"]
    C4 --> P2["make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m<br/>Rg-Dmax-Ree joint distribution"]
    C3 --> P3["graph.py<br/>Rg / Dmax / Ree histograms"]
    C2 --> P4["plotEOMSAXScomparison.m<br/>fit + Kratky + residuals"]
    C2 --> P5["graph.py<br/>SAXS fit curve"]
    C5 --> P6["2d.py<br/>Rg-Ree scatter highlight"]
```

Since each consumer is documented in its own page, use the following routes to continue: the complete field-by-field specification of every output file lives in [GAJOE Output File Reference](9-gajoe-output-file-reference); the frequency-extraction logic sketched above is fully developed in [Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles](10-best-curve-reconstruction-from-ga-cycles); the fit/Kratky/residual plots belong to [SAXS Fit, Kratky Plot, and Residuals](13-saxs-fit-kratky-plot-and-residuals); and the Jensen-Shannon divergence computed between the full MD pool and GAJOE's refined ensemble is covered in [2D Ensemble Comparison Histograms](11-2d-ensemble-comparison-histograms). To understand where GAJOE's inputs come from, go one step upstream to [FFMAKER Theoretical SAXS Profiles](7-ffmaker-theoretical-saxs-profiles).


# GAJOE Output File Reference



This page is the canonical field guide to the files GAJOE v2.x writes after an Ensemble Optimization Method (EOM) run, documented against the concrete example shipped in this repository (`ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1`). For the algorithm itself, see [GAJOE Genetic Algorithm Ensemble Fitting](8-gajoe-genetic-algorithm-ensemble-fitting); for how these files are produced from a pool, see [FFMAKER Theoretical SAXS Profiles](7-ffmaker-theoretical-saxs-profiles). Every format described here is verified against the actual example files and against the MATLAB/Python parsers in this repo that read them.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L12-L17), [README.md](/README.md#L90-L97)

## Output Directory Layout and Naming

GAJOE creates one output directory per invocation — `GA001`, `GA002`, etc. — and one `curve_N` subdirectory per experimental dataset fitted. The example folder contains 100 `GA_CYCLE_N.txt` workfiles (one per independent GA repeat), a fitted profile, four structural distribution files, the pool descriptor table, and one non-GAJOE companion file (`Ree_values.mat`, added by the analysis workflow). Note that `pdbs/` and `logFile_*.log` appear in fresh GAJOE runs (per the tutorial) but are omitted from this archived example.

```mermaid
graph TD
    GA["GA001/"] --> C1["curve_1/"]
    C1 --> FIT["profiles_001_1.fit<br/>(fitted SAXS profile)"]
    C1 --> CYC["GA_CYCLE_1.txt … GA_CYCLE_100.txt<br/>(GA workfiles)"]
    C1 --> DIST["Rg_distr_001_1.txt<br/>Size_distr_001_1.txt<br/>CaCa_distr_001_1.txt<br/>Volume_distr_001_1.txt"]
    C1 --> SL["Size_list.txt<br/>(pool descriptors)"]
    C1 --> REE["Ree_values.mat<br/>(user-generated, not GAJOE)"]
```

| File(s) | Content | Written by | Primary consumer in repo |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GA_CYCLE_1.txt` … `GA_CYCLE_100.txt` | Per-generation ranked ensembles for each GA run | GAJOE (opt-in) | `getBestCurve.m` |
| `profiles_001_1.fit` | q-grid, experimental I(q), error, fitted ensemble I(q) | GAJOE | `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m`, `graph.py` |
| `Rg_distr_001_1.txt`, `Size_distr_001_1.txt`, `CaCa_distr_001_1.txt`, `Volume_distr_001_1.txt` | Pool vs. selected-ensemble distributions | GAJOE | `graph.py` (pattern-based) |
| `Size_list.txt` | Per-structure Rg and Dmax for the full pool | GAJOE | `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` |
| `Ree_values.mat` | End-to-end distances (variable `R`) | User workflow | `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` |
| `pdbs/`, `logFile_*.log` | Selected conformations; run log | GAJOE | `2d.py` (pdbs only) |

The numeric suffixes `_001_1` carry dataset and curve indices; the authoritative linkage to a specific GA cycle is stored *inside* the file headers, not in the file names.

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L90-L97), [ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1)

## GA_CYCLE_N.txt — Genetic Algorithm Workfiles

Each `GA_CYCLE_N.txt` records one complete independent GA run. Line 1 is the header `Gener Best`; the remainder consists of one block per generation (1000 blocks here), each listing 20 ranked candidate ensembles from rank 20 down to rank 1. A row encodes: generation number, rank, the ensemble's chi², and the ensemble membership as pool-structure indices delimited by hyphens — e.g. `-156-359-734-792-792-805-812-1159-1166-`, where a repeated index means that conformation appears multiple times in the ensemble. The chi² trajectory is visible directly in the file: the best ensemble in generation 1 of cycle 1 scores 16.43, converging to 1.37 by generation 1000.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["GA_CYCLE_N.txt<br/>hyphen-delimited rows"] --> B["readmatrix<br/>Delimiter = '-'"]
    B --> C["Keep last rows =<br/>final generation ranks 1..20"]
    C --> D["Flatten + drop NaN<br/>(rank/generation text)"]
    D --> E["tabulate structure indices"]
    E --> F["best_curve =<br/>[PDB index, frequency]"]
```

Critically, these files only exist if you answered **yes** to GAJOE's prompt *"Save workfiles with the entire GA runs? (default: no)"* — `getBestCurve.m` documents this requirement because GAJOE v2 removed the `best_curve.txt` summary that version 1.3 emitted. The parser reads each file with `readmatrix(..., "Delimiter", '-')`, keeps the final `curvesPerEnsemble` rows (the last generation's ranked list), flattens the matrix to a column, and discards `NaN` cells (which is where the non-numeric "chi²:" text lands), then tabulates how often each pool structure occurs across those top-ranked ensembles. The resulting `best_curve = [PDBnums, freqnums]` matrix is the join key into `Size_list.txt` and `Ree_values.mat` downstream.

> [!TIP]
> Without the workfiles opt-in, a GAJOE v2.x run leaves you with no machine-readable record of *which* structures were selected — `getBestCurve.m` exists precisely to reconstruct the lost `best_curve.txt` from `GA_CYCLE_*.txt`. This is elaborated in [Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles](10-best-curve-reconstruction-from-ga-cycles).

Sources: [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L21), [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L19982-L20001), [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L4-L17), [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L28-L42)

## profiles_001_1.fit — Fitted Scattering Profile

The `.fit` file is the primary quantitative artifact: the ensemble-averaged theoretical curve GAJOE selected as the best fit, evaluated on the experimental q-grid. Line 1 is a single-line header echoing the run configuration; lines 2+ are four-column numeric data (53 rows here, exactly matching the 53-point experimental dataset declared in `H4WT_150Na.dat`).

| Header field (example value) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CYCLE: 29` | The independent GA run whose ensemble produced this fit |
| `Chi^2: 1.226` | Goodness-of-fit of the winning ensemble |
| `GENER.: 1000` | Generations per run |
| `ENSEMBLES: 50` | Candidate ensembles evaluated per generation |
| `CURVES: 9` | Conformations in the winning ensemble |

The data columns are `q`, experimental `I(q)`, error, and fitted `I(q)`. Both consumers treat it the same way structurally: `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m` reads it with `NumHeaderLines=1` and uses columns 1 and 4 for the fit overlay, while `graph.py` unpacks all four as `q, exp, err, fit`. Note that the header's cycle (29) differs from cycle 1's best chi² (1.37) — the stored fit comes from the best-performing cycle among all runs, which is why the file name suffix alone cannot identify the source cycle.

> [!TIP]
> The error column in `.fit` is GAJOE-processed, not a copy of the raw experimental errors: at low q the example shows ~10⁻¹⁷ values versus 10⁻³ in `H4WT_150Na.dat`. That is why `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m` deliberately re-reads the raw experimental `.dat` (with `NumHeaderLines=4`) for its error bars and interpolates experimental intensities onto the `.fit` q-grid when computing residuals. This pipeline is covered in [SAXS Fit, Kratky Plot, and Residuals](13-saxs-fit-kratky-plot-and-residuals).

Sources: [profiles_001_1.fit](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/profiles_001_1.fit#L1-L4), [H4WT_150Na.dat](/SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat#L1-L4), [plotEOMSAXScomparison.m](/plotEOMSAXScomparison.m#L10-L22), [graph.py](/Example_tutorial/graph.py#L26-L30)

## *_distr_001_1.txt — Structural Distributions

All four distribution files share one schema: four summary lines reporting pool and selected-ensemble statistics (average and histogram-derived values), a column-header line, then three-column binned data: bin value, normalized pool frequency, and normalized selected-ensemble frequency. These are the files to consult for a quick read of whether the GA shifted the ensemble's structural landscape — for example, the Rg file shows the ensemble average rising to 15.27 Å against a pool average of 13.77 Å, a direct fingerprint of the SAXS-driven selection pressure.

| File | Bin variable | Ensemble avg | Pool avg |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Rg_distr_001_1.txt` | Radius of gyration (Å) | 15.27 | 13.77 |
| `Size_distr_001_1.txt` | Dmax (Å) | 47.33 | 42.69 |
| `CaCa_distr_001_1.txt` | Ca(N)–Ca(C) end-to-end distance (Å) | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| `Volume_distr_001_1.txt` | Excluded volume | 0.00 | 0.00 |

> [!TIP]
> The CaCa and Volume distributions are **all zeros in this workflow** — the FFMAKER statistics for this pool were generated without end-to-end distances. The repository compensates by measuring Ree externally from pool PDBs into `Ree_values.mat` (via `pdb_Rmeas.m`), which `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` then loads as variable `R`, index-aligned with `Size_list.txt`. Do not treat the zeroed CaCa bins as a physical result; the structural concept is covered in [Structural Descriptors: Rg, Dmax, Ree](16-structural-descriptors-rg-dmax-ree).

Sources: [Rg_distr_001_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Rg_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L6), [Size_distr_001_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L5), [CaCa_distr_001_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/CaCa_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L5), [Volume_distr_001_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Volume_distr_001_1.txt#L1-L5)

## Size_list.txt — Pool Descriptor Table

`Size_list.txt` is the flat, one-row-per-conformation descriptor table for the entire RANCH/MD pool: column 1 is the 1-based structure index (1–2000 here, matching the 2001-line file), column 2 is Rg, and column 3 is Dmax. This index is the shared namespace for the whole output directory: the hyphen-delimited integers inside `GA_CYCLE_*.txt` ensembles reference these row numbers, and `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` relies on that alignment when it maps each selected structure to its descriptors via `Sizelist(bestcurve(n,1), 2:3)` and to its end-to-end distance via `R(bestcurve(n,1))`. Any downstream tool that joins GAJOE outputs must preserve this 1-based indexing convention.

Sources: [Size_list.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L15), [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](/make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L25-L34), [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](/make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L38-L50)

## Companion Files Not Written by GAJOE

Three artifacts in or around the output directory come from outside GAJOE proper, and knowing their provenance prevents misconfiguration. **`Ree_values.mat`** is generated by the analysis workflow (running `pdb_Rmeas.m` over the full pool's structures) and is the only source of end-to-end distances in this pipeline, given the zeroed `CaCa_distr` file. **`pdbs/`** — present in fresh GAJOE runs per the tutorial — holds the selected conformations as CIF/PDB; `2d.py` consumes it by globbing file stems and intersecting them against FFMAKER's `size_statistics_20.csv` to build the Rg–Ree scatter with selected structures highlighted ([Rg-Ree Scatter Plot with Marginals](15-rg-ree-scatter-plot-with-marginals)). **`logFile_*.log`** records the interactive GAJOE session settings and results. Finally, the experimental `.dat` files in `SAXSData/` (4-line headers, tab-separated q/I/error) are the fitting targets that `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m` reads alongside the `.fit` output.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](/make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L2-L4), [2d.py](/Example_tutorial/2d.py#L6-L30), [README.md](/README.md#L90-L97), [H4WT_150Na.dat](/SAXSData/H4WT_150Na.dat#L1-L4)

## File-Consumption Map

The following diagram consolidates how every output file flows into the repository's analysis tooling, which is useful when wiring up a new GAJOE run: the workfiles feed ensemble membership, `Size_list.txt` + `Ree_values.mat` feed pool descriptors, and the `.fit` file pairs with the raw experimental data for scattering-level comparison.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph GAJOE["GAJOE outputs (GA001/curve_1/)"]
        CYC["GA_CYCLE_*.txt"]
        FIT["profiles_001_1.fit"]
        SL["Size_list.txt"]
        DISTR["*_distr_001_1.txt"]
    end
    subgraph COMP["Companion inputs"]
        REE["Ree_values.mat"]
        DAT["SAXSData/*.dat"]
    end
    CYC --> GBC["getBestCurve.m"]
    GBC -->|"best_curve [index, freq]"| M2D["make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m"]
    SL --> M2D
    REE --> M2D
    M2D --> O1["2D histograms + Jensen-Shannon divergence"]
    FIT --> PLT["plotEOMSAXScomparison.m"]
    DAT --> PLT
    PLT --> O2["SAXS fit, Kratky plot, residuals"]
    FIT --> GP["graph.py"]
    DISTR -.->|"*_distr_*.dat glob"| GP
```

| Consumer script | Reads | Produces | Catalog page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getBestCurve.m` | `GA_CYCLE_*.txt` | `best_curve` matrix | [Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles](10-best-curve-reconstruction-from-ga-cycles) |
| `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` | `best_curve`, `Size_list.txt`, `Ree_values.mat` | 2D histograms, JSD | [2D Ensemble Comparison Histograms](11-2d-ensemble-comparison-histograms), [Jensen-Shannon Divergence Quantification](12-jensen-shannon-divergence-quantification) |
| `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m` | `profiles_001_1.fit`, `SAXSData/*.dat` | Fit, Kratky, residual plots | [SAXS Fit, Kratky Plot, and Residuals](13-saxs-fit-kratky-plot-and-residuals) |
| `graph.py` | `profiles_*.fit`, `*_distr_*.dat` | SAXS and distribution plots | [SAXS Curve and Distribution Plots](14-saxs-curve-and-distribution-plots) |
| `2d.py` | `pdbs/*.cif`, `size_statistics_20.csv` | Rg–Ree scatter with marginals | [Rg-Ree Scatter Plot with Marginals](15-rg-ree-scatter-plot-with-marginals) |

Sources: [README.md](/README.md#L15-L17), [graph.py](/Example_tutorial/graph.py#L34-L47), [2d.py](/Example_tutorial/2d.py#L6-L30)

## Practical Notes and Cross-Version Behavior

Three implementation details matter when adapting these parsers to your own GAJOE runs. First, version behavior: GAJOE v2.x removed the `best_curve.txt` summary file, so the repository standardizes on GAJOE v2.1 plus `getBestCurve.m` for ensemble membership extraction — running v1.x or later v2.x releases may shift prompts and file naming. Second, the `graph.py` distribution globs target `*_distr_*.dat`, while the archived example stores distributions as `*.txt`; the reader is defensive (`if not files: continue`) and its header-skipping `read_numeric` helper tolerates either layout, but be aware the distribution plots may silently be skipped on an extension mismatch. Third, header-line counts are contract-critical in MATLAB: experimental `.dat` files use 4 header lines (`NumHeaderLines=4`) while `.fit` files use 1 — off-by-one here shifts every column and corrupts the comparison silently rather than raising an error.

To go deeper, run the tutorial yourself in [EOM Tutorial with ATSAS Tools](4-eom-tutorial-with-atsas-tools), then follow the consumers in order: [Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles](10-best-curve-reconstruction-from-ga-cycles) → [2D Ensemble Comparison Histograms](11-2d-ensemble-comparison-histograms) → [SAXS Fit, Kratky Plot, and Residuals](13-saxs-fit-kratky-plot-and-residuals). For the end-to-end application of these outputs to a real benchmark, continue to [H4 Histone Tail Case Study](17-h4-histone-tail-case-study).


# Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles



This page documents `getBestCurve.m`, the MATLAB utility that reconstructs the composition of the genetic-algorithm solution across all independent GAJOE cycles — a two-column table of conformational-pool indices and their selection frequencies. When ATSAS upgraded from GAJOE 1.3 to v2.x, the automatic `best_curve.txt` export disappeared; this function restores that capability by parsing the per-cycle workfiles that GAJOE v2–3 optionally saves. The page covers the workfile format the parser depends on, the reconstruction algorithm, the function contract, a worked example against the repository's bundled GAJOE output, and how the result connects to the rest of the analysis pipeline.

## Why This Script Exists: The GAJOE 1.3 → 2.x Regression

GAJOE is the genetic-algorithm engine of the Ensemble Optimization Method: it selects weighted sub-ensembles from a conformational pool whose averaged theoretical SAXS profile best fits the experimental data. GAJOE 1.3 wrote the composition of its solution directly to a `best_curve.txt` file. GAJOE v2–3 removed that export, but it retained an option to save the complete genetic-algorithm history as workfiles — provided the user explicitly enables it during the GAJOE session:

```
> Save workfiles with the entire GA runs? (default: no) ................ : y
```

The function's own header states its purpose plainly: *"Take output from GAJOE v2-3 and extract PDB numbers in all ensembles — Essentially recreates the best_curve.txt file generated from gajoe 1.3 that was removed from gajoe 2 for SOME reason"* ([getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L2-L13)). If this option was not selected during the GAJOE run, no `GA_CYCLE_*.txt` files exist and the function has nothing to parse — this is the single most common failure mode, addressed in the troubleshooting table below.

## Anatomy of a GA_CYCLE Workfile

Each independent GA run produces one workfile named `GA_CYCLE_<run>.txt` in the GAJOE output folder (the repository ships a complete example with runs 1 through 100 under `ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/`, alongside the standard GAJOE outputs such as `profiles_001_1.fit` and `Rg_distr_001_1.txt`) ([README.md](/README.md#L91-L98)). The workfile is one long log of the optimization: every generation records its top 20 ranked candidate ensembles, each line carrying four semantic fields:

```
Gener  Best
    1   20) chi^2: 35.26 - ensemble:  -122-180-257-374-751-953-1093-1382-1382-1509-1509-1944-1990-
```

The integers in the `ensemble` field are **indices into the RANCH conformational pool**, not PDB file names — the bundled example uses a 2,000-structure pool, indexed 1–2000, whose per-structure Rg and Dmax values are tabulated in `Size_list.txt` ([Size_list.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L6)). The example run converges dramatically: the first generation's rank-20 candidate sits at χ² = 35.26, while the final (1000th) generation's population spans only χ² ≈ 1.37–1.43 ([GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L3), [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L19982-L20001)).

This raw format is hostile to naive parsing: field separators (`-`) collide with the negative-sign convention of the ensemble list, ranks and χ² values are embedded in free text, and ensembles have variable member counts (5–15 in the example). The function sidesteps all of this with a single deliberate choice — parsing with `-` as the column delimiter, so every line decomposes into alternating numeric and non-numeric columns:

| Raw token(s) | Parsed column content | Survives NaN filter? |
|---|---|---|
| `1000` (generation) | numeric, but discarded context | Removed by tail-slice, not NaN |
| `1) chi^2: 1.37` | non-numeric text → NaN | No — stripped at [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L22-L23) |
| `ensemble:` label | non-numeric text → NaN | No — stripped |
| `858`, `1093`, `1463`… | pool indices | **Yes — kept** |
| trailing `-` → empty cell, short-row padding | NaN fill | No — stripped |

Sources: [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L3), [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L19-L23)

> [!TIP]
> **Delimiter choice as robustness mechanism.** Because `readmatrix` with `"Delimiter", '-'` converts every non-numeric token (generation text, χ² strings, the `ensemble:` label) to NaN, and NaN-pads every row to the widest row's width, the single `~isnan` filter at [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L23) simultaneously removes headers, metadata, variable-width padding, and stray trailing blank lines. The parser never needs to know how many members an ensemble has — the data self-identifies as "the columns that are numbers."

## The Reconstruction Algorithm

The function executes a five-stage pipeline. Stages 1–3 run once per GA cycle; stages 4–5 aggregate across all cycles:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["GA_CYCLE_1.txt … GA_CYCLE_n.txt<br/>(one per independent GA run)"] --> B["Stage 1 — readmatrix<br/>Delimiter '-' → mixed columns, non-numerics become NaN"]
    B --> C["Stage 2 — tail slice<br/>keep last curvesPerEnsemble rows<br/>= final generation, ranks 20→1"]
    C --> D["Stage 3 — flatten + strip<br/>reshape to column, remove NaN<br/>leaving only pool indices"]
    D --> E["Stage 4 — concatenate<br/>stack indices from all nRuns cycles"]
    E --> F["Stage 5 — tabulate<br/>categorical conversion + frequency count"]
    F --> G["best_curve = PDB index × frequency<br/>two-column N×2 matrix"]
```

**Stage 1–3, per cycle.** The loop constructs each filename from the run number, reads it with the dash delimiter, then takes exactly the last `curvesPerEnsemble` rows: `raw(end-(curvesPerEnsemble-1):end,:)`. Since a workfile ends with the final generation's complete ranked population, this slice isolates the converged solution — rank 20 through rank 1 of the last generation. The slice is flattened column-wise and filtered through `~isnan`, yielding a clean column vector of pool indices ([getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L19-L23)).

**Stage 4–5, global.** All cycles' index vectors are vertically concatenated into one master list, converted to `categorical`, and passed to `tabulate`, which produces unique-value/counts pairs. The extraction loop pulls the numeric indices and their frequencies into parallel arrays, and the function returns them bound as an N×2 matrix — one row per distinct pool structure that ever appeared in any converged ensemble, column 1 the pool index, column 2 its total occurrence count ([getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L25-L39)).

## Function Signature and Parameters

```matlab
best_curve = getBestCurve(dir, nRuns, curvesPerEnsemble)
```

| Parameter | Type | Meaning | Example value (bundled data) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | char | Directory containing the `GA_CYCLE_i.txt` workfiles — the `curve_*` subfolder of the GAJOE output | `'ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1'` |
| `nRuns` | scalar | Number of independent GA cycles saved by GAJOE; drives the filename loop `GA_CYCLE_1..n` | `100` |
| `curvesPerEnsemble` | scalar | Ranked ensembles retained from each file's tail — must equal the rank population GAJOE reports per generation (20 in the example format) | `20` |
| `best_curve` (return) | N×2 double | Column 1: pool index (1–2000 in the example pool); column 2: occurrence count across all cycles | — |

Sources: [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L2), [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L19-L21)

## Worked Example Against the Repository Data

The bundled `ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/` folder contains exactly 100 workfiles (one per `--times` GA run) from a 2,000-structure pool with 1,000 generations and a 20-ensemble ranked population each. The correct invocation is:

```matlab
best_curve = getBestCurve('ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1', 100, 20);
```

The result aggregates 100 runs × 20 converged ensembles ≈ 1,600 ensemble slots (before multiplicity expansion), so the frequency column reflects how strongly each pool structure is drawn into χ² ≈ 1.4 solutions across independent restarts — a far more stable statistic than any single run's rank-1 pick, because genetic-algorithm selection is stochastic and different runs can weight different near-equivalent conformers. To interpret indices structurally, join column 1 against `Size_list.txt`, whose first column is the same pool index and whose remaining columns give that structure's Rg and Dmax ([Size_list.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L6)).

## Interpreting the Output: Multiplicity and Population-Wide Aggregation

Two semantic subtleties determine correct use of the output. First, frequencies are **occurrence-weighted, not binary**: GAJOE permits repeated structures within an ensemble (note rank 1 of the final generation, where index `1734` appears four times — `-858-1093-1463-1734-1734-1734-1734-`), and every repetition contributes a count ([GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L20001)). The frequency column therefore encodes selection *weight* — how much of the fitted ensemble's scattering mass each conformer carries — which is precisely what a `best_curve.txt` composition record must preserve. Second, the function aggregates the **entire final-generation population** (all 20 ranks), not merely the single best ensemble. This is a deliberate statistical choice: by generation 1000, all ranked members are converged near-solutions (χ² spread of only 1.37–1.43 in the example), so pooling them characterizes the full solution manifold rather than betting on one stochastic winner.

> [!TIP]
> **Frequencies are composition weights, not probabilities over structures.** Because repetition counts multiplicatively and each ensemble slot contributes, the sum of the frequency column equals the total member count across all retained ensembles — not the number of distinct structures. When comparing against the full MD ensemble downstream (e.g., for divergence calculations), treat the counts as weights over pool indices; do not normalize by N rows.

Sources: [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L29-L39), [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](/ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L19982-L20001)

## Prerequisites, Pitfalls, and Troubleshooting

The function assumes a specific GAJOE configuration and MATLAB environment. The GAJOE prerequisite is non-negotiable — workfiles are only written when the save option is answered `y` ([getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L7-L9)), and the repository notes MATLAB R2021 or later may be required ([README.md](/README.md#L23-L25)); the frequency stage additionally relies on `tabulate`, which ships with the Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox rather than base MATLAB.

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `readmatrix` error or empty `best_curve` | GA_CYCLE workfiles never written | Re-run GAJOE answering `y` to *"Save workfiles with the entire GA runs?"* ([getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L7-L9)) |
| Indices exceed pool size / frequencies look wrong | `dir` pointed at the GAJOE parent folder instead of the `curve_*` subfolder where workfiles live | Point `dir` at `.../GA001/curve_1` (matching the bundled example layout) |
| Output counts implausibly small | `curvesPerEnsemble` smaller than the actual rank population — tail slice silently discards converged rows | Set it to the ranked-ensemble count per generation (20 in the example format) |
| Crash in the `tabulate` stage | `nRuns` exceeds the number of saved cycles, producing an empty index vector | Match `nRuns` to the actual `GA_CYCLE_*.txt` count (100 in the example) |
| MATLAB errors on `tabulate` | Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox not installed | Install the toolbox, or replace the counting block with an equivalent `unique(...)`/`histcounts` pattern |

Sources: [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L7-L9), [getBestCurve.m](/getBestCurve.m#L16-L30), [README.md](/README.md#L23-L25)

## Where This Fits in the Pipeline

`getBestCurve.m` occupies the post-GAJOE analysis tier of the workflow: it converts GAJOE's raw optimization history into an explicit, machine-readable solution composition that the rest of the MATLAB toolchain and the pool statistics can consume. The averaged intensity curve itself — the actual "best fit" plotted against experiment — comes from GAJOE's `profiles_*.fit` output and is handled separately by `plotEOMSAXScomparison.m`, which reads the fit file and renders the SAXS overlay, Kratky form, and residuals ([README.md](/README.md#L15-L17), [plotEOMSAXScomparison.m](/plotEOMSAXScomparison.m#L9-L17)).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["RANCH pool"] --> F["FFMAKER profiles"] --> G["GAJOE genetic fitting"]
    G --> W["GA_CYCLE workfiles<br/>(workfiles option = y)"]
    W --> B["getBestCurve.m<br/>index × frequency table"]
    B --> S["join Size_list.txt<br/>Rg / Dmax per selected structure"]
    S --> H["2D histograms & JSD<br/>vs. full MD ensemble"]
    G --> P["profiles_*.fit<br/>averaged fitted curve"] --> K["plotEOMSAXScomparison.m<br/>fit / Kratky / residuals"]
```

For the conceptual machinery upstream — how GAJOE's genetic algorithm samples and scores ensembles, and what each workfile and distribution file contains — see [GAJOE Genetic Algorithm Ensemble Fitting](8-gajoe-genetic-algorithm-ensemble-fitting) and [GAJOE Output File Reference](9-gajoe-output-file-reference).

## Suggested Next Steps

Having reconstructed the solution composition, the natural progression within the MATLAB Analysis Scripts section is:

- [2D Ensemble Comparison Histograms](11-2d-ensemble-comparison-histograms) — feed the SAXS-refined ensemble (via these selections) and the full MD pool into the 2D comparison plots produced by `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m`
- [Jensen-Shannon Divergence Quantification](12-jensen-shannon-divergence-quantification) — quantify how far the GA-selected distribution sits from the parent MD distribution
- [SAXS Fit, Kratky Plot, and Residuals](13-saxs-fit-kratky-plot-and-residuals) — visualize the averaged fitted curve from `profiles_001_1.fit` that complements this composition-level view


# 2D Ensemble Comparison Histograms



This page documents `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` (repository root), the MATLAB script that visualizes how a SAXS-refined EOM ensemble deviates from the full MD conformational pool in joint two-dimensional descriptor space — **Rg vs Ree** and **Rg vs Dmax** — using joint scatter panels flanked by marginal histograms. The script also prints mean ± standard-error statistics and computes the **Jensen-Shannon divergence** between pool and ensemble distributions. A lightweight Python equivalent, `Example_tutorial/2d.py`, produces the Rg–Ree panel for the ATSAS tutorial workflow. Everything here assumes GAJOE v2.1 output has already been generated.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L1-L18), [README.md](README.md#L15-L17), [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L1-L9)

## Where This Script Sits in the Workflow

`make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` is the **post-GAJOE visualization stage** of the pipeline: it consumes GAJOE's raw text outputs, reconstructs which pool structures the genetic algorithm selected and how often, then overlays that frequency-weighted ensemble on the full pool. The scientific question it answers is direct: *does fitting the SAXS curve bias conformational selection toward more compact or more extended members of the pool?* The repository README states this explicitly — once GAJOE results are generated, run this script to generate the 2D comparison histogram and calculate the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the two distributions.

The script was adapted in May 2024 for GAJOE v2.1, which no longer emits a `best_curve.txt` file; the missing piece is reconstructed on the fly by the sibling function `getBestCurve.m`, covered in detail in [Best-Curve Reconstruction from GA Cycles](10-best-curve-reconstruction-from-ga-cycles).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph GAJOE["GAJOE v2.1 output — curve_1/"]
        GAC["GA_CYCLE_1..100.txt<br/>per-run GA logs (PDB IDs per ensemble)"]
        SL["Size_list.txt<br/>per-structure: index, Rg, Dmax"]
    end
    subgraph EXT["External prerequisites"]
        RV["Ree_values.mat<br/>Ree per pool structure<br/>(produced by pdb_Rmeas.m)"]
        BC["getBestCurve.m"]
    end
    subgraph WS["Workspace structs"]
        POOL["pool: .rg, .dmax, .r"]
        GAJ["gajoe: .rg, .dmax, .r<br/>frequency-weighted rows"]
    end
    subgraph OUT["Outputs"]
        F1["Figure 1 — Rg vs Ree + marginals"]
        F2["Figure 2 — Rg vs Dmax + marginals"]
        ST["Mean ± SEM per descriptor (console)"]
        JS["JSD values for Rg and Ree (console)"]
    end
    GAC --> BC
    BC --> GAJ
    SL --> POOL
    RV --> POOL
    POOL --> F1 & F2 & ST & JS
    GAJ --> F1 & F2 & ST & JS
```

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L1-L10), [README.md](README.md#L15-L17), [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L1-L12)

## User-Defined Parameters

All configuration lives in the first code block under `%% User-defined parameters` — per the README, running either MATLAB analysis script mostly amounts to matching the paths here. The defaults are calibrated to the bundled example dataset (`ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1`, 100 GA runs, 20 curves per ensemble, 2000-structure pool).

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1` | Path to a single GAJOE results directory |
| `nRuns` | `100` | Number of repeated GA runs ("Number of times you want the genetic algorithm repeated") |
| `curvesPerEnsemble` | `20` | Maximum number of curves per ensemble, as entered in GAJOE |
| `xlim_Dmax` | `[20 80]` | X-axis limits (Å) for the Dmax panel and its marginal |
| `ylim_Rg` | `[5 30]` | Y-axis limits (Å) shared by both figures' Rg axes |
| `xlim_R` | `[0 80]` | X-axis limits (Å) for the Ree panel and its marginal |
| `gajoeHistBins` | `15` | Bin count for the EOM-ensemble overlay histograms |
| `binsRg`, `binsDmax`, `binsR` | `22` each | Bin counts for the full-pool histograms and the JSD computation |
| `fontSize`, `axisFontSize` | `33`, `22` | Publication-quality label and axis tick font sizes |

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L13-L27), [README.md](README.md#L17)

## Input Contract: Files the Script Reads

The script binds to specific GAJOE v2.1 artifacts plus one externally generated file. Each has a strict column layout that the parsing code depends on.

| File | Producer | Content used | Parsed as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Size_list.txt` | GAJOE (EOM pool stage) | One row per pool structure | Column 2 → `pool.rg`, column 3 → `pool.dmax` (column 1 is the structure index) |
| `Ree_values.mat` | External: `pdb_Rmeas.m` run over all full-pool PDBs | Variable `R` — end-to-end distance per structure | `pool.r = R(1:end)` |
| `GA_CYCLE_<i>.txt` | GAJOE v2.1 (requires workfiles saved) | Final-generation ensemble compositions, `-`-delimited PDB IDs | Flattened by `getBestCurve` into `[PDB number, frequency]` pairs |

The bundled example shows the `Size_list.txt` format concretely: row `1 → 9.25 → 26.79` means structure 1 has Rg = 9.25 Å and Dmax = 26.79 Å, and the file holds 2001 rows for a 2000-structure pool. A single `GA_CYCLE` file contains one ranked block of candidate ensembles (with their χ² scores) per GA generation — e.g. line `1 1) chi^2: 16.43 - ensemble: -156-359-734-792-...-` is generation 1's best ensemble, listing member PDB IDs delimited by dashes.

> [!TIP]
> The `GA_CYCLE_*.txt` files only exist if you answered **yes** to GAJOE's prompt *"Save workfiles with the entire GA runs? (default: no)"* — the default `no` will make `getBestCurve` fail with a missing-file error before any plotting begins.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L30-L42), [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L7-L27), [Size_list.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/Size_list.txt#L1-L15), [GA_CYCLE_1.txt](ExampleData/H4_tail_WT_ff19SB_OPC/GA001/curve_1/GA_CYCLE_1.txt#L1-L21)

## From GA Cycles to a Weighted Ensemble Representation

The core data transformation is **frequency-weighted expansion** of the selected ensemble. `getBestCurve` returns a two-column matrix — PDB structure number and how many times the GA selected it across all runs and all final-generation candidate ensembles. The plotting script then converts each `(structure, frequency)` pair into that many identical rows of `(Dmax, Rg, Ree)` via `repmat`, producing the `gajoe` struct whose distributions reflect selection weight, not just membership:

```matlab
for n = 1:gaj
    D_Rep = repmat(Sizelist(bestcurve(n,1),3),bestcurve(n,2),1);
    Rg_Rep = repmat(Sizelist(bestcurve(n,1),2),bestcurve(n,2),1);
    R_Rep = repmat(R(bestcurve(n,1)),bestcurve(n,2),1);
    Dmax_gaj = [Dmax_gaj; D_Rep]; Rg_gaj = [Rg_gaj; Rg_Rep];
    R_gaj = [R_gaj; R_Rep];
end
gajoe.dmax = Dmax_gaj; gajoe.rg = Rg_gaj; gajoe.r = R_gaj;
```

The `pool` struct, by contrast, holds exactly one row per structure — an unweighted baseline. Every overlay in the figures and every statistical comparison (means, SEM, JSD) is therefore *weighted ensemble vs. uniform pool*.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L45-L55), [getBestCurve.m](getBestCurve.m#L19-L39)

## Anatomy of the Two Figures

Both figures use a **3×3 subplot canvas trick**: the main joint panel occupies cells `[4,5,7,8]` (bottom-left 2×2 block), the top marginal histogram occupies `[1,2]`, and the right marginal occupies `[6,9]`. The right marginal is rendered horizontally then rotated into place with `set(gca,'xdir','reverse')` and `camroll(-90)`, so Rg increases outward from the joint panel. Full-pool points are drawn as MATLAB's default orange dots (`[0.8500 0.3250 0.0980]`) and EOM-selected structures as open blue circles (`[0.3010 0.7450 0.9330]`, `LineWidth` 2), with a `NorthWest` legend reading "full pool" / "selected by EOM".

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph CANVAS["550×550 figure canvas (3×3 subplot grid)"]
        TOP["Cells [1,2]<br/>Top marginal histogram<br/>Ree (Fig 1) or Dmax (Fig 2)"]
        MAIN["Cells [4,5,7,8]<br/>Joint panel<br/>orange dots = full pool<br/>blue circles = selected by EOM"]
        RIGHT["Cells [6,9]<br/>Right marginal: Rg histogram<br/>xdir reversed + camroll(-90)"]
    end
    MAIN --- TOP
    MAIN --- RIGHT
```

The two figures differ only in the horizontal descriptor:

| Aspect | Figure 1 | Figure 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Joint panel axes | `R_ee (Å)` vs `R_g (Å)` | `D_max (Å)` vs `R_g (Å)` |
| Top marginal variable | `pool.r` / `gajoe.r` | `pool.dmax` / `gajoe.dmax` |
| Pool marginal bins | `binsR = 22` / `binsRg = 22` | `binsDmax = 22` / `binsRg = 22` |
| Ensemble overlay bins | `gajoeHistBins = 15` | `gajoeHistBins = 15` |
| Marginal normalization (Fig 1 only) | Peak-normalized: `BinCounts / max(BinCounts)` | Not normalized |

Note the normalization asymmetry: in Figure 1 the September 2025 revision peak-normalizes every marginal so pool and ensemble histograms are shape-comparable regardless of sample size, while Figure 2's marginals remain raw counts. Also, pool and ensemble overlays deliberately use different bin counts (22 vs 15), so visual overlap comparisons are qualitative.

> [!TIP]
> When adapting the axes limits (`xlim_Dmax`, `ylim_Rg`, `xlim_R`) to a new protein, recall that all three variables are reused across both figures and their marginals — a single edit re-scales the entire visualization, but values outside the limits are silently clipped from the display.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L58-L111), [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L134-L180)

## Statistical Summary Printed to the Console

After Figure 1, the script prints mean Rg, mean Ree, and the **standard error of the mean** (`std/sqrt(n)`) for both the full pool and the EOM-selected ensemble to the MATLAB command window. The equivalent Dmax block is present but commented out, and these are plain string expressions rather than formatted output — they appear as quoted character arrays on separate lines. This console summary complements the figure: the 2D panel shows *where* the ensemble shifts, the marginal shapes show *how broadly*, and the mean ± SEM quantifies whether the shift exceeds sampling noise.

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L116-L130)

## Built-in Jensen-Shannon Divergence

The final section quantifies the visual comparison. For each of Rg and Ree, both distributions are binned with `'Normalization','pdf'` (proper probability densities, unlike the peak-normalized display histograms), and the divergence is computed as `JSD = H(0.5·p1 + 0.5·p2) − 0.5·H(p1) − 0.5·H(p2)`, where `H` is Shannon entropy over natural log (`p.*log(p)` with NaN terms zeroed so empty bins contribute nothing). The method is credited in the comments to `plotIterativeAnalysis.m` from RNA-condensate analysis software, and was added in September 2025. Results `JSD_rg` and `JSD_r` print to the console as unsuppressed expressions.

A JSD near 0 means the SAXS-refined ensemble statistically mirrors the MD pool; larger values indicate selection bias toward specific conformational sub-populations. The full mathematical treatment, properties (bounded by `ln 2` for natural-log JSD), and interpretation guidance live in the dedicated page [Jensen-Shannon Divergence Quantification](12-jensen-shannon-divergence-quantification).

Sources: [make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m](make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m#L185-L234)

## The Python Alternative: `Example_tutorial/2d.py`

The tutorial folder ships a compact Python implementation of the Rg–Ree panel, designed for the 20-structure ATSAS demo rather than the large MATLAB pipeline. Its selection-identification strategy differs fundamentally from the MATLAB route: instead of reconstructing frequencies from `GA_CYCLE` logs, it globs the CIF filenames GAJOE deposited in `GA001/curve_1/pdbs/` and builds a boolean mask against the pool's filename column — so each selected structure is drawn once, unweighted. It parses FFMAKER's `size_statistics_20.csv` (fields 1, 3, and 6 in the whitespace-split line: Rg, Ree, structure filename), and asserts that every globbed selection exists in the pool file.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["size_statistics_20.csv<br/>(FFMAKER)"] --> C["rg, ree arrays"]
    B["GA001/curve_1/pdbs/*.cif<br/>(GAJOE selection)"] --> D["boolean mask"]
    C --> E["Rg–Ree scatter +<br/>density-normalized marginals"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["EOM_2D.png (300 dpi)"]
```

The figure uses a `GridSpec(2,2)` with `width_ratios=[4,1.3]`, `height_ratios=[1.3,4]` — the Pythonic analogue of the MATLAB 3×3 trick — with shared axes (`sharex`/`sharey`), coral for the pool, open dodgerblue circles for selections, `density=True` histograms over 12 `np.linspace` bins, and no console statistics or JSD.

| Capability | `make2Dplot_fromEOMresults.m` | `2d.py` |
|---|---|---|
| Panels | Rg–Ree **and** Rg–Dmax figures | Rg–Ree only |
| Selection source | `GA_CYCLE` logs via `getBestCurve` (frequency-weighted) | `pdbs/*.cif` glob (binary mask, unweighted) |
| Marginal normalization | Peak-normalized (Fig 1) / raw counts (Fig 2) | Density-normalized (`density=True`) |
| Console statistics | Mean ± SEM for Rg, Ree | Selected-structure name list + count assert |
| JSD computation | Yes (Rg and Ree) | No |
| Output | Two MATLAB figures + console | `EOM_2D.png` at 300 dpi |

Sources: [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L8-L41), [Example_tutorial/2d.py](Example_tutorial/2d.py#L44-L107), [README.md](README.md#L100-L118)

## Running the Analysis Step by Step
